items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: He wrote a tune called “Afrique” with Count Basie and he actually used that theme and made a tune out of it.

ctx.x: Wow. You and I — not to get off the track but I noticed you and I share a love of Hubert Laws.

Oh yeah. And I actually did my doctoral paper on Hubert. And I’ve met him several times because he did a lot of work for Dad. He played on the Count Basie “Afrique” album, he played on an album called “The Mayor Speaks” and Dad wrote a suite for strings and jazz orchestra and Hubert played on that. Then he did some television stuff that he would go to L.A. and play. He actually played my first Bundy flute and that was a real treat. So I got a chance to kind of catch back up with him, and actually he was © Fillius…

playing with the Smithsonian, that was a couple of years ago, and I got a chance to actually present my paper to him and I gave him a copy of it. And it was really neat because he said, “This is one of the best papers on me that I’ve ever seen.”
